newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine alumina workers may get 30.8% share.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine alumina workers may get 30.8% share.

text.p: A Ukrainian government commission has concluded that workers at the country's sole alumina plant should be allowed to acquire 30.8 percent of its shares under privatisation, according to the State Property Fund.

Fund chairman Yuri Yekhanurov told reporters at the weekend that the recent signing of an agreement assessing the value of the Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod between the fund and its leaseholders would pave the way for sale of the plant.
The country's highest court last month denied the workers' collective the right to own a 40.14 percent stake in the plant, located in the Black Sea port of Mikolayiv.
The company is one of 208 state-owned large enterprises that Ukraine plans to put out for tender in an attempt to attract $1 billion from foreign strategic investors.
The court case had effectively halted the property fund, the state agency overseeing privatisation, from privatising the alumina producer, which has a nominal value of $178 million.
A fund spokesman said previously that the government planned to keep at least 25 percent plus one share in the plant and investors might be able to purchase 20-25 percent.
The company has forecast its output at 1.0 million tonnes in 1996, compared to 996,000 tonnes in 1995.

The Mikolayiv plant receives most of its bauxite from the West African country of Guinea and sends 90 percent of its output to Russian aluminium smelters. The remainder goes to Ukraine's only smelter at Zaporizha.
